translations.text: Draw me after you; let us run. Bring me, O king, into your chamber. We will rejoice and delight in you. We will remember your love more than wine, and I have loved you more than the upright.
See, you are beautiful, my beloved; see, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves.
Like lilies among thorns, so is my beloved among the young women.
I charge you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or the deer of the field: do not awaken or stir up love until it wishes.
On my bed at night I sought the one my soul loves. I sought him, but I did not find him.
Your teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep coming up from washing. All of them bear twins, and none of them is bereaved.
Your neck is like David’s tower, built with [?]. A thousand shields hang on it, all the shields of mighty warriors.
You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride. You have captivated my heart with one of your eyes, with a single necklace around your neck.
Your navel is a round bowl that never lacks mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat surrounded by lilies.
If only you were like a brother to me, nursing [?] at the breasts of my [?]! I would find you in the street and kiss you, and they would not despise me.
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken for?
